description: We are building a single-storey motel in Red Deer. Guest rooms open directly to the outside (no interior corridors). There is a full basement used for laundry and storage. The building area is 380 m2 and the basement is also 380 m2. Slab-on-ground basement floor; main-floor joists span 4.3 m from the Part 9 span tables; stick-framed lumber rafters, 4.0 m clear span (no roof trusses); no sprinkler system is proposed; the building official has not asked for professional drawings.
known_facts: exterior-access guest rooms, no interior corridors
full basement for laundry and storage

gold.engineering_reason: Code exception passes: building height is 1 storey (a basement is below the first storey) and building area 380 m2 is within 400 m2 (Div C 2.4.1.1.(1)(c)(i)). The Acts measure gross area: read as a single-storey building, gross area including the basement is 760 m2 (> 400 m2, Architects Act s.2(6)(c)(i)); read as a 2-storey building, each floor is 380 m2 (> 200 m2, s.2(6)(c)(ii)). Either reading fails the exception, so a registered architect (authorized entity) is required (s.2(1)); EGPA s.2(7)(c) is identical.
gold.limit_source: Architects Act s.2(1), s.2(6)(c)(i)-(ii); EGPA s.2(7)(c); Div C 2.4.1.1.(1)(c)(i); Div A 1.4.1.2.(1) Building area / Basement / Building height definitions.

authoring.label: model-constructed, model-checked, not human-verified
authoring.notes: Constructed scenario, not a real case. Gold written from the quoted sources before any system run. Not human-reviewed. Code building-area vs Act gross-area divergence.

assumptions: "Gross area" is not defined in either Act (both PDFs searched). Gold assumes the basement counts either toward gross area or as a storey; a third reading (gross area = above-grade area only, basement ignored) would let the Acts' exception pass. Human confirmation advised before headline use.

Main floor serves only guest rooms (residential areas) with exterior access, chosen so Div B 9.23.4.1.(2) (non-residential floor spans) is not triggered; laundry/storage basement treated as ancillary.
